title: Quire packet drawers with a rolling word-slip tray and a context-conditioned letter jig
method: A 15th-century copyist carries one rolling word-slip tray, a deeper reserve and a reusable letter jig. At each new quire packet the same physical stock is replenished from neighboring pages of a public practice transcript, using a fixed 18-page packet and a 3.5% card refresh chance per written word. On a turn the writer draws a whole-word slip from the recently written line or page, then from the active packet, or sets a fresh spelling with the letter jig learned from public training pages; ordinary one- and two-glyph copying slips are resolved through local context-conditioned letter cards. The preceding word can guide the next card through the shared edges of slips in the public letter table; a separate card position is used at the beginning and end of a written line. The drawers are reloaded in manuscript order and retained for a packet before the next packet is reached. A page or paragraph boundary clears the short rolling tray, as when a copyist changes leaf or starts a new passage. Card choice uses no semantic categories, section labels, Currier labels, or rule about any target glyph, length, repetition count or page statistic. This single setting and seed were fixed before the practice score was read.
